topic: Sexual health screening in psychiatric inpatients

audits.title: An Audit Cycle Highlighting the Rate of Chlamydia Screening in a Forensic Child and Adolescent Mental Health Unit in Birmingham
audits.standard: National Chlamydia Screening Programme recommendation to screen at-risk young people
audits.setting: Forensic Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (FCAMHS) Ardenleigh, Birmingham; three adolescent forensic wards (2 medium secure, 1 low secure)

cycle1.result: 11.5% of patients tested for chlamydia although 36.8% met screening criteria; physical health (Rethink) form completed in 73.7%

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit (details not stated)
audits.other_findings: Physical health forms were no longer in use by the re-audit; the authors suggest adding chlamydia screening to admission processes.
audits.citation: Ugalahi T, Hassan H, O'Brien J. An Audit Cycle Highlighting the Rate of Chlamydia Screening in a Forensic Child and Adolescent Mental Health Unit in Birmingham. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S179-S180.

audits.title: Improving Women's Sexual and Reproductive Health in Acute Inpatient Psychiatric Services – A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Current national guidance on sexual and reproductive health (not named)
audits.setting: Female acute psychiatric inpatient ward, later extended to a neighbouring ward

cycle1.result: 12.5% of inpatients offered at least one of contraceptive counselling, cervical and breast screening or STI screening.

audits.intervention: Women's health assessments with provision of emergency contraception and STI swabs, sexual health clinic referral protocol, dedicated clinic time, poster and leaflet, and an outcome proforma, over six PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: 87.7% offered a leaflet and 63.1% offered counselling; 48.8% of these accepted at least one intervention.

audits.other_findings: Dedicated clinic time gave the highest offer rate (94.1%, cycle 3); compliance fell to 54.2% at junior doctor changeover. Neighbouring ward offers rose from 28.6% to 63.6%; seven STIs were detected and treated.
audits.citation: Tulip S, Godsell S, Roche S, Okay A, Hartshorn K. Improving Women's Sexual and Reproductive Health in Acute Inpatient Psychiatric Services – A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S175-S175. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.446.

audits.title: An Audit of Sexual Health Screening Practices on the General Adult Female Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: NICE guidelines and Trust Clinical Policy SD29 for physical health care (target 100%)
audits.setting: Four general adult female psychiatric inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Valid annual physical health check 94% (none fully complete); cancer screening covered in 55% of eligible, sexual health history 55%, menstrual history 22%, obstetric and gynaecology history 12%; pregnancy test on admission 48%; STI screening considered in 13%; sexual health counselling offered to 11%; 90% lacked contraceptive discussion beyond oral contraception.

audits.other_findings: 25% non-completion of pregnancy tests in over-45s, likely due to undocumented menopausal status. Staff teaching, policy updates and wider policy distribution were suggested.
audits.citation: Farakish L, Elbadrawy T, Desai R, Hyland D. An Audit of Sexual Health Screening Practices on the General Adult Female Inpatient Wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S244-S244. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10606.

audits.title: Sexual History Taking in Acute Psychiatric Inpatient Admissions: An Audit of Documentation and Clinician Practice
audits.standard: Devon Partnership NHS Trust Sexual Safety Policy (C60); NICE, CQC and Sexual Safety Collaborative guidance
audits.setting: Haytor Ward, acute psychiatric inpatient ward, Devon Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Documentation of sexual health and sexual safety below expected Trust standards (figures not reported). 50% of surveyed doctors aware of the policy.

audits.other_findings: No sexual health section in the admission clerking proforma; the s1 template missed policy elements such as gender identity and history of sexual harm. Template improvement and training recommended.
audits.citation: Ali R, Lopes A, Ahmed F, Ceylan D. Sexual History Taking in Acute Psychiatric Inpatient Admissions: An Audit of Documentation and Clinician Practice. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S277-S277. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11560.

audits.title: Increasing routine HIV testing in low and medium secure forensic settings
audits.standard: National standards: routine HIV testing on admission in high-prevalence areas
audits.setting: Five low and seven medium secure male forensic wards, West London NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 30.6% (56/183) offered an HIV test or had a result recorded; 23.5% had results available.

audits.intervention: Education of patients and staff, HIV testing added to routine admission primary care screening, and separate consent forms removed.

cycle2.result: 82.6% (154/184) offered or tested; 43.4% had results available.

audits.other_findings: Tests offered without a result rose from 7.1% to 39.1%; 17.4% still had neither.
audits.citation: Swain R, Dujic M, Leung T. Increasing routine HIV testing in low and medium secure forensic settings. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S223-S223.
